claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Despite enthusiasm for multi-agent LLM systems, their performance gains on popular benchmarks are often minimal.
claims.quote: Despite enthusiasm for Multi-Agent LLM Systems (MAS), their performance gains on popular benchmarks are often minimal.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The paper introduces MAST-Data, a dataset of over 1600 annotated traces collected across 7 popular multi-agent system frameworks.
claims.quote: We introduce MAST-Data, a comprehensive dataset of 1600+ annotated traces collected across 7 popular MAS frameworks.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: MAST-Data is described as the first multi-agent system dataset to outline failure dynamics in multi-agent systems for guiding better future systems.
claims.quote: MAST-Data is the first multi-agent system dataset to outline the failure dynamics in MAS for guiding the development of better future systems.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The authors build the first Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy, called MAST, to systematically classify failures in MAST-Data.
claims.quote: To enable systematic classification of failures for MAST-Data, we build the first Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy (MAST).

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: MAST was developed through analysis of 150 traces, guided by expert human annotators and validated with high inter-annotator agreement of kappa = 0.88.
claims.quote: We develop MAST through rigorous analysis of 150 traces, guided closely by expert human annotators and validated by high inter-annotator agreement (kappa = 0.88).

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The taxonomy identifies 14 unique failure modes clustered into 3 categories: system design issues, inter-agent misalignment, and task verification.
claims.quote: This process identifies 14 unique modes, clustered into 3 categories: (i) system design issues, (ii) inter-agent misalignment, and (iii) task verification.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: To enable scalable annotation, the authors develop an LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline with high agreement with human annotations.
claims.quote: To enable scalable annotation, we develop an LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline with high agreement with human annotations.
